summary: Port reproduces the six-mode structure and the flagship expanding-rainbow-ripple look, but runs every mode ~11% fast, snaps hue mid-ripple, and gets three of the six modes visibly wrong (mode 1 blacks out, mode 3's wave runs vertical instead of diagonal, mode 4's dark well is ~3x too small, mode 5's palette too bright).
observations: Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one slider named 'sliderMode' (label 'Mode'), and a 25-point sweep (b-0.02 .. b-0.98) puts the mode boundaries at the same slider values on both sides - 6 discrete modes with breaks at 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6, 5/6.

Both sides are 2D patterns on a 3D rig: on the default 5x5x5 cloud every group of 25 pixel indices renders identically, i.e. the output is invariant along one lattice axis on BOTH sides. The pattern clearly expects a square 2D panel map we don't have; that is a rig caveat, identical on both sides, not a port defect. Structural work below was therefore done on --rig grid (16x16/24x24/32x32) and --pixels 1000, which both sides get equally.

Mode 0 (default, slider 0-1/6): both draw a rainbow-gradient ring expanding from the panel centre, hue increasing ~+10 deg per pixel of radius, fading out past the corners and respawning. Radial speed is IDENTICAL: on a 16x16 grid the peak goes r=1.6 -> r=9.9 in 1.80 s on both sides.

Cycle period is the port's biggest systematic error: original repeats every 3.28 s, port every 2.94 s (~11% fast). Measured three ways - ring restarts over 20 s (orig 3.25/3.30/3.30/3.20/3.30 s, port 2.90/3.00/2.90/3.00/2.90 s), mode-3 flash peaks (orig 1.20/4.45/7.75/11.00 s, port 2.20/5.15/8.05/11.00 s), and the cloud-rig brightness super-period (orig 6.55 s, port 5.90 s). Both sides are fps-invariant (same periods at --fps 10, 20 and 40), so this is not frame-rate coupling, just a wrong time constant.

Mode 0 ring width: original's ring is broader. Radial brightness profile at matched radius (~r=14.5 on a 32x32 grid) gives FWHM ~5.0 px for the original vs ~3.8 px for the port; at r~7, ~4.8 px vs ~3.8 px. Whole-run mean brightness follows: orig 20-22, port 16.

Mode 0 hue discontinuity (port only): every ~6.6 s the port's ring flips hue by ~-170 deg in a single frame while at full brightness and mid-flight - e.g. the brightest pixel goes (0,88,221) blue at t=6.50 s to (244,151,0) orange at t=6.55 s. Seen at t=6.55, 13.15 and 19.65 s in a 20 s window. The original's hue advances smoothly (~90 deg/s) through every ripple and only changes base between ripples.
Mode 0 ripple start-hue sequence: original strictly alternates between ~14 deg and ~110 deg (111, 12, 107, 18, 111, 12 over six ripples); port drifts (95, 172, 77, 155, 59, 137).

Long-window colour balance differs: over 240 s untouched the original averages R 18.8 / G 12.7 / B 27.6, the port R 8.7 / G 15.4 / B 24.5 - the port renders roughly half the original's red. Same skew on the grid rig (orig R 15.1 / G 19.8 / B 31.9 vs port R 7.8 / G 18.5 / B 21.7). Brightness-weighted hue histograms over 27 sampled frames: original has a clear red/orange lobe (0-60 deg = 11.5% of energy) and a hole at 60-90 deg; the port has almost nothing at 0-60 deg (1.8%) and peaks in cyan/blue instead.

Mode 1 (slider 1/6-2/6, sweeping rainbow bar): both draw a rainbow bar sweeping across the panel, but the original is CONTINUOUSLY lit - meanBrightness stays in 16..21 for all 240 frames of a 12 s window, min 16 - while the port pulses from 0 to 21 on a 2.95 s cycle and sits at or near black about a quarter of the time (66/240 zero-motion frames, meanBrightness min 0). Port mean 9.5 vs orig 18.6. The original's rhythm image shows two crossing families of sweeps forming a continuous lattice; the port's shows one family separated by wide black gaps.

Mode 2 (slider 2/6-3/6): both dim - a single small blob/streak drifting and changing colour. Original's blob is a larger elongated streak (mean 2.1), the port's is a more compact dot (mean 1.1). Closest of the six modes after mode 0.

Mode 3 (slider 3/6-4/6, orange sweep flash) is a structural divergence: dumping the peak frames on a 24x24 grid shows the original's band is a 45-degree DIAGONAL wave (constant along x+y, travelling diagonally), while the port's band is VERTICAL (constant down each column, travelling in x only). Confirmed on two separate peaks per side (orig t=1.20/4.45, port t=2.20/5.15). Port's band is also brighter and narrower (peak meanBrightness 47-48 vs 34-35).

Mode 4 (slider 4/6-5/6, light-blue field with a dark orbiting well): field colour matches exactly (RGB ratio 0.30/0.58/1.00 on both) and both wells orbit the panel in ~3 s, but the port's well is far too small - pixels below half brightness are 277-289 of 1024 (~28%) on the original vs 28-32 of 1024 (~3%) on the port, i.e. roughly a third of the radius. Field mean brightness 107 (orig) vs 149 (port).

Mode 5 (slider 5/6-1): both render a completely static (motion 0) four-colour diagonally-shifting block texture, but the palettes differ. Original: (229,0,27) bright, (13,0,0), (0,0,13), (0,0,0) - reads as red-on-black. Port: (255,0,76) bright, (101,0,0), (0,40,101), (0,0,0) - the two 'dark' entries are 8x brighter, so the port reads as pink with clearly visible dark-red and navy blocks. Mean 58 (orig) vs 79-80 (port). Block run lengths also differ (orig mixes 1-5 px runs with a 2 px checker, port is uniform 4 px runs).

Not a defect: both sides are seed-independent (seed 1 and seed 1234 render the same character) and neither degrades - a --skip 200 window at t=200-212 s shows both still alive with unchanged means (orig 22.2, port 16.0).

dials.name: sliderMode
dials.origEffect: Selects one of 6 modes at slider = k/6: (0) expanding rainbow ripple from centre, 3.28 s repeat; (1) continuously-lit rainbow bar sweeping across; (2) dim drifting colour streak; (3) orange 45-degree diagonal wave flashing past every 3.28 s; (4) light-blue field with a large dark well (28% of panel below half brightness) orbiting in ~3 s; (5) static red-on-black four-colour block texture.
dials.portEffect: Same 6 modes at the same slider boundaries, but: (0) ripple is ~25% thinner and repeats every 2.94 s with a ~170-degree hue snap mid-flight every 6.6 s; (1) bar pulses to black on a 2.95 s cycle instead of staying lit; (2) blob more compact and dimmer; (3) wave is VERTICAL, not diagonal, and repeats every 2.94 s; (4) dark well only ~3% of panel, field 40% brighter; (5) same static texture idea but with much brighter dark palette entries (pink/navy instead of near-black).

feedback: Global timing: every mode's repeat cycle is ~11% too fast - 2.94 s against the original's 3.28 s (measured identically at 10, 20 and 40 fps, so it is a time constant, not a frame-step). The ring's radial SPEED already matches exactly; what differs is that the original holds the new ring at r~0 for ~0.7 s before it starts moving while the port only holds it ~0.35 s. Lengthen that birth dwell (or the cycle length) by ~0.34 s and mode 0, 3 and 4 timings all land.

Mode 0 hue snap: the port's ring hue base jumps by about -170 degrees in one frame, mid-flight, every 6.6 s (t=6.55, 13.15, 19.65 s at seed 1) - a fully-lit blue ring turns orange in a single frame. The original never does this: its hue advances smoothly at ~90 deg/s through a whole ripple and only changes base at the moment a new ripple is born. The base hue should be latched per-ripple, not driven off a separate clock.

Mode 0 ripple start hue: original alternates strictly between ~14 and ~110 degrees on successive ripples (a clean two-ripple colour alternation); the port's start hue drifts (95, 172, 77, 155, 59, 137). The visible effect is that the original cycles between two recognisable colour families while the port wanders.

Mode 0 ring width: the original's ring is ~30% wider - FWHM ~5.0 px vs ~3.8 px on a 32x32 grid at matched radius. Widening the radial falloff also fixes the ~20% overall brightness shortfall (orig mean 20-22, port 16).

Colour balance overall: the port renders about half the original's red over long windows (240 s untouched: orig R/G/B 18.8/12.7/27.6, port 8.7/15.4/24.5). Each of the original's ripples sweeps ~300 degrees of hue including a pass through red/orange; the port's sweep is shorter (~245 degrees) and usually stops before red.

Mode 1 (slider ~0.25): the original's bar is on-screen continuously - mean brightness never drops below 16 over 12 s, and its rhythm shows two crossing sweep families. The port applies mode 0's birth/death brightness envelope to this mode as well, so it blacks out for roughly a quarter of every 2.95 s cycle (66/240 frames with zero motion, min brightness 0). Drop the envelope here and keep the bar lit.

Mode 3 (slider ~0.55): wrong wave direction. The original's orange band is constant along x+y and travels diagonally at 45 degrees; the port's band is constant down each column and travels horizontally. Confirmed by dumping both sides' brightness peaks on a 24x24 grid. The port's band is also narrower and brighter (peak mean 47 vs 34) - widen and dim it once the direction is fixed.

Mode 4 (slider ~0.75): the dark well is far too small. On a 32x32 grid the original keeps ~283/1024 pixels (28%) below half brightness with a smooth gradient reaching r~13; the port only ~30/1024 (3%) reaching r~7. Roughly triple the well's radius. The blue field colour and the ~3 s orbit are already correct.

Mode 5 (slider 1.0): the static texture's two dark palette entries are ~8x too bright - original uses (13,0,0) and (0,0,13) (both read as black, so the panel looks red-on-black), the port uses (101,0,0) and (0,40,101) (visible dark-red and navy blocks over a pink field). Also the port's block runs are a uniform 4 px while the original mixes 1-5 px runs with a 2 px checker.
